doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

chapter: Jazz players and the record industry
title: The Fillius Jazz archive and its value
summary: Gold praises the archive for letting young people learn; Rowe notes 500 sessions online.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And where does it end? I don't know. And you're archiving the whole thing, which is great. So anybody who's interested can go back and look at all these great musicians and composers and arrangers and I don't know are you doing singers too? You're doing everything? Yeah. So that's wonderful. You know? I mean because at least if a kid is interested in learning they'll have something to go and listen to. You know you should put it up — do you have an internet channel that you have them on?
We do. It's called Fillius Jazz and there's 500 sessions up there.
You'll be — I think it's 504 or so.

There you go. So you know they have something they can go look, if they find a name that all of a sudden if they find Bernard Purdie, oh, what's up, he invented a shuffle? Oh let me go put his name in. And then they can get a hit off of that. You know what I mean? It's like that's important stuff. It's like that makes this as respectful as classical music was. You know? Where I read something recently about the history of the cello. You know that was written like 75 years ago. You know? And it was fascinating to me. You know? But I'm a cellist so it would be fascinating. But I still took the energy to read it. © Fillius Jazz Archive 18
